worked: Married filing combined (joint federal), ages 66 and 60. Person 0 has the Social Security and person 1 the public pension: the group is evaluated for each person, so both are kept. A single choice for the whole return would lose one of them. Federal taxable Social Security: other income 100,000.00 + half of benefits 15,000.00 = provisional 115,000.00; 85% x (115,000.00 - 44,000.00) + 6,000.00 = 66,350.00, limited to 85% x 30,000.00 = 25,500.00. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = pensions 30,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 + interest 70,000.00 = 125,500.00. Federal taxable income = 125,500.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (including the additional amount for age 65) = 92,400.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 125,500.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 125,500.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 125,500.00 - 0.00 = 125,500.00. MO-A Part 3 Section C (Y, age 66): Line 1 25,500.00; Line 3 25,500.00 (62 or older by December 31). Section C Line 4 total 25,500.00. Section A (S): Line 1 30,000.00; Line 2 lesser of that or 47,633.00 = 30,000.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 4 30,000.00. Section A Line 5 total 30,000.00. Projection, best_of_group evaluated for each person separately: person 0: larger of Social Security exemption 25,500.00 and public pension 0.00 = 25,500.00; person 1: larger of Social Security exemption 0.00 and public pension 30,000.00 = 30,000.00; total 55,500.00, the same as Section A Line 5 + Section C Line 4. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 55,500.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for age 65 or older = 33,100.00. Line 26 subtotal 125,500.00 - 55,500.00 - 33,100.00 = 36,900.00. Line 29 taxable income 36,900.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 1,313.00 = 26.26 + 2.5% x 1,313.00 = 32.825 + 3% x 1,313.00 = 39.39 + 3.5% x 1,313.00 = 45.955 + 4% x 1,313.00 = 52.52 + 4.5% x 1,313.00 = 59.085 + 4.7% x 27,709.00 = 1302.323; total 1558.358 = 1,558.36. The form itself splits this: Line 5 Y 25,500.00, S 100,000.00 (the return-level income taken as S's); Line 7 20% / 80%; Line 27 7,380.00 and 29,520.00; Lines 30Y and 30S 177 + 1211 = 1388 on Line 36. The projection applies the chart once to the couple's total, so expected is 1,558.36. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 125,500.00 - Line 8 55,500.00 = 70,000.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 125,500.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.

Married filing combined: Missouri figures a separate tax for each spouse on that spouse's share of taxable income, using the one chart twice, and this is required, not chosen. The projection applies the chart once to the couple's total taxable income, because the format has no way to say tax is per spouse.

The public pension exemption and the Social Security exemption share a best_of_group, each person separately. Form MO-A takes the lesser of the pension or 47,633 and subtracts that person's Social Security exemption (Section A Lines 2-4), which reduces the exemption, not the cap, so cap_reduced_by would be wrong. The two exemptions together come to the larger of the Social Security exemption and the lesser of the pension or 47,633, which is what the group gives when evaluated per person.
